reason: The order approves the Code of Fair Competition for the Cast Iron Soil Pipe Industry under Title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act; its operative words are "do order that the said Code of Fair Competition be and it is hereby approved". Under section 3 of Title I an approved code supplied the standards of fair competition (3(b)), equity enforcement by the district courts (3(c)) and criminal liability for violations (3(f)), so the command had no operative effect apart from section 3. Section 2 of Senate Joint Resolution 113, approved on the date stated in the resolution as "Approved, June 14, 1935.", provides that all the provisions of Title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act delegating power to the President to approve or prescribe codes of fair competition and providing for the enforcement of such codes "are hereby repealed"; the resolution states no other effective date for section 2. The approval therefore ceased to operate on June 14, 1935. A. L. A. Schechter Poultry Corp. v. United States, decided May 27, 1935, is recorded as a validity characterization (the section 3 code-making delegation was held unconstitutional; under the doctrine then prevailing an approval made under it was void from issuance), not as an end date, because no held record shows that the government cancelled or suspended this code on that date. June 16, 1935, the original two-year expiry of Title I, is not an end: section 1 of the resolution replaced that expiry with "on April 1, 1936", and nothing in the resolution defers section 2.
